'''Nicolas Bergeron''' (19 December 1975 – 15 February 2024) was a French mathematician who worked in [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] in Paris.

== Early career  ==
Bergeron obtained his PhD at [[École normale supérieure de Lyon]] in the year 2000 under the supervision of [[Jean-Pierre Otal]]. His thesis was titled ''Cycles géodésiques dans les variétés hyperboliques'' ("geodesic cycles in hyperbolic varieties").<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=59363|title=Nicolas Bergeron – The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=www.mathgenealogy.org}}</ref>

== Work ==
Bergeron's main interests concerned the geometry and topology of locally symmetric spaces and arithmetic groups, as well as their [[cohomology]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sites.google.com/view/nicolasbergeron/accueil|title=His webpage}}</ref> and their connection to number theory, in particular to Hilbert's 12th problem.<ref> {{Cite arXiv|title=Elliptic units for complex cubic fields (on Eisenstein's Jugendtraum)| last1=Bergeron | first1=Nicolas | last2=Charollois | first2=Pierre| first3=Luis|last3=García| date=2023|class=math.NT |eprint=2311.04110 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |language=en |title=video link "On Eisenstein's Jugendtraum for complex cubic fields" 9-3-2023 |url=https://archive.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/id/eprint/4899/ |website=[[Max Planck Institute]]|date=March 2023 }}<!-- auto-translated from French by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

Some of his publications showed an interest in [[Oulipo]], referencing [[An Attempt at Exhausting a Place in Paris]] by [[Georges Perec]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cnrs.fr/fr/recherche/prix/docs/BergeronN.pdf|title=''L'arithmétique des formes''|date=10 January 2024 }}</ref> He also wrote a (non-mathematical) article about [[Jacques Roubaud]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://images.math.cnrs.fr/Quelques-vies-plus-ou-moins-breves-de-Jacques-Roubaud?lang=fr|title=Images des mathématiques|website=images.math.cnrs.fr}}</ref>

Bergeron was latterly a member of the editorial board of the journal [[Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS]].<ref name="IHES 2023">{{cite web | title=The Publications mathématiques de l'IHES | website=IHES | date=11 January 2023 | url=https://www.ihes.fr/en/library/les-publications-mathematiques-de-lihes/ | access-date=14 April 2023}}</ref>

== Death ==
Bergeron died on 15 February 2024, at the age of 48.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tribute to Nicolas Bergeron (1975 – 2024) |url=https://www.ihes.fr/en/tribute-to-nicolas-bergeron-1975-2024/ |website=IHES |date=16 February 2024 |access-date=18 February 2024}}</ref>

* {{cite journal | last1=Bergeron | first1=Nicolas | last2=Wise | first2=Daniel T. | title=A Boundary Criterion for Cubulation | journal=American Journal of Mathematics | publisher=The Johns Hopkins University Press | volume=134 | issue=3 | year=2012 | issn=0002-9327 | jstor=23240564 | pages=843–859 | doi=10.1353/ajm.2012.0020 | arxiv=0908.3609 | url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/23240564 | access-date=22 November 2022}}
* {{cite web | title=Exposé Bourbaki 1055 : La conjecture des sous-groupes de surfaces d'après Jeremy Kahn et Vladimir Markovic | website=Société Mathématique de France | url=https://smf.emath.fr/publications/expose-bourbaki-1055-la-conjecture-des-sous-groupes-de-surfaces-dapres-jeremy-kahn-et | language=fr | access-date=22 November 2022}}

* Bergeron edited a few articles for the site ''Images des mathématiques'' du CNRS.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://images.math.cnrs.fr/_nicolas-bergeron_.html?lang=fr|title=Images des mathématiques|website=images.math.cnrs.fr}}</ref>

* with [[Akshay Venkatesh]]: The asymptotic growth of torsion homology for arithmetic, groups, J. Inst. Math Jussieu 12 (2013), no.2, 391-447.

* with [[John Millson (mathematician)|John Millson]] and [[Colette Moeglin]]: The Hodge conjecture and arithmetic quotients of complex balls, Acta Math. 216 (2016), no. 1, 1–125.

* With 14 co-authors, ''Uniformisation des surfaces de Riemann'' ("Uniformization of Riemann Surfaces").<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://math.univ-lille1.fr/~popescu/InfoENS_SaintGervais.pdf|title=ENS Éditions}}</ref><ref>''Henri Paul de Saint-Gervais'' is the pseudonym of a group of 15 mathematicians, working together for a week in 2007 at [[Saint-Gervais-la-Forêt]], in Sologne : [[Aurélien Alvarez]], [[Christophe Bavard]], [[François Béguin]], Nicolas Bergeron, [[Maxime Bourrigan]], [[Bertrand Deroin]], [[Sorin Dumitrescu]], [[Charles Frances]], [[Étienne Ghys]], [[Antonin Guilloux]], [[Frank Loray]], [[Patrick Popescu-Pampu]], [[Pierre Py]], [[Bruno Sévennec]] et [[Jean-Claude Sikorav]].</ref>

==Awards and prizes==
* Bergeron won the ''Médaille de bronze du CNRS'' in 2007<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cnrs.fr/fr/recherche/prix/bronze/2007.htm|title=Palmarès 2007}}</ref>

* Bergeron was a junior member of [[Institut Universitaire de France]] from 2010 until 2015<ref>{{cite web|title=Nicolas Bergeron|url=https://www.iufrance.fr/les-membres-de-liuf/membre/1031-nicolas-bergeron.html|editor=Institut universitaire de France|website=iufrance.fr|language=fr|access-date=1 May 2021|publication-date=}}</ref>

* Bergeron was an invited speaker at the 2018 [[International congress of mathematicians]] in Rio with a talk on "Hodge theory and cycle theory of locally symmetric spaces"<ref>{{Citation
| last         = Bergeron
| first        = N.
| contribution = Hodge theory and cycle theory of locally symmetric spaces
| year         = 2018
| title        = Proceedings of the international congress of mathematicians, ICM 2018, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, August 1–9, 2018. Volume II. Invited lectures.
| publisher    = Hackensack, NJ: World Scientific; Rio de Janeiro: Sociedade Brasileira de Matemática
}}</ref>

* Bergeron was a Takagi lecturer in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ms.u-tokyo.ac.jp/~toshi/jjm/JJM_HP/contents/takagi/21st/21stPoster.pdf|title=Takagi lectures |date=2018}}</ref>

* Bergeron was a Aisenstadt chair lecturer in Montréal in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.crmath.ca/activites/#/type/activity/id/3765| title=Aisenstadt chair 2020}}</ref>

* Bergeron received the Prix fondé par l'Etat from French Académie des Sciences in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Laureats/laureat-2023-du-prix-fonde-par-l-etat-nicolas-bergeron.html| title=Prix 2023}}</ref>
